name: Village Enterprise (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The locations the sheet's bottom line reads (row labels naming Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda), sharing equally.

missing_data.note: Partly thin (50%): Village Enterprise counts its participants and their consumption before and after, but with no comparison group; the share of the rise the programme caused is our judgment, anchored on the randomised trial of the same programme.

summary: Village Enterprise trains groups of three people in extreme poverty in rural Kenya, Rwanda and Uganda to run a small business, gives each a cash grant and sets up savings groups. The Life You Can Save puts the income gain at 3.92 dollars per dollar spent, the average of the three countries' rise in household consumption between Village Enterprise's baseline and endline surveys over the programme's 2023/24 cost. Our view counts only the part of that rise the programme caused, which we judge from the randomised trial of the same programme, lets the gain last several years, and values it like every income gain on the site; the biggest uncertainty is that share.

The three countries' programme costs
People times the rise in ln(consumption) per dollar, the three countries pooled by their money
rows.formula: (cost_kenya * roi_kenya * consumption_share_kenya * ln_per_gain_dollar_kenya + cost_rwanda * roi_rwanda * consumption_share_rwanda * ln_per_gain_dollar_rwanda + cost_uganda * roi_uganda * consumption_share_uganda * ln_per_gain_dollar_uganda) / cost_sheet
rows.explainer: Each country's return per dollar, consumption only, turned into ln(consumption) for the people in the household, weighted by the money spent in each country; the sheet's plain average counts the three countries equally.

rows.label: Share of the baseline-to-endline rise the programme caused
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 8% (3% to 25%); the sheet counts the whole rise. The sheet's figures compare participants before and after, with no comparison group, and its own comment says the rise can't all be put down to the programme. Anchor: the randomised trial of Village Enterprise's programme in Kenya and Uganda (Sedlmayr, Shah and Sulaiman 2020) found household consumption about 7% higher in Kenya and 4% in Uganda than in control villages at follow-up (ln gains of about 0.07 and 0.04), against rises of 108% and 119% (ln 0.73 and 0.78) in this monitoring; the share is the trial's gain over the monitoring's, with room for a bigger effect in today's programme.

rows.label: Yearly fade of the consumption gain
rows.explainer: Our judgment: businesses and savings groups set up in the programme year keep earning, with some closing each year. The sheet counts one year.

rows.label: Years the consumption gain lasts, counted from the programme year
rows.explainer: Our judgment, as in our own model of Village Enterprise: the businesses and savings groups keep raising consumption for some years after the programme year. The sheet counts one year.

rows.label: Years of the gain, fading and discounted to today
rows.explainer: The gain's years at the discount rate under Your values, fading each year.

rows.label: Deaths averted by higher incomes, as a share of the consumption benefit
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: aid_value): higher household incomes avert some child deaths; multiplied by the value-of-a-life slider. The sheet counts income only.

rows.label: Benefits to non-participants, as a share of participants' benefits
rows.explainer: A side effect, our judgment 10% (0 to 40%): new businesses buy from and hire neighbours; the trial measured no harm to non-participants. The sheet counts participants only.

rows.label: Village Enterprise's spending outside the three countries' programme costs, per dollar of them
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 20% (5% to 40%). The sheet's costs are the country programmes' capital and recurrent costs; a dollar given to Village Enterprise also pays its management and fundraising, which were 19% of its total expenses in its 2025 accounts (programme expenses 17.1 of 21.0 million dollars, Form 990), and we can't tell how much of that the sheet's costs already include.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of programme cost
rows.explainer: The shared default for programmes where staff deliver the help themselves (business mentors train and coach the groups); the cash grants are the other large part.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: The shared default for delivery staff hired locally.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Full cost per dollar of the sheet's costs
rows.explainer: The sheet's costs plus central costs and, with credit by share of resources on, staff's forgone pay.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.formula: ln_per_dollar_pooled * attributable_share * persistence_pv * $uov_per_ln_consumption * (1 + income_mortality_uov_ratio * $life_value_multiplier + spillover_ratio) / cost_multiplier
rows.explainer: The ln(consumption) gain the programme caused, over its years, valued like every income gain on the site, with the deaths higher incomes avert and the gains to neighbours, per dollar of the full cost.
